cases.title: The Last Page
cases.tagline: A famous novelist is dead behind a door that was locked from the inside.
cases.author: Interrogation Room Team

setting.location: Vell House, Heron Island (reachable only by passenger ferry)
setting.atmosphere: A cold, windy evening. The last ferry leaves the island at 22:10.
setting.summary: Bestselling author Marcus Vell was writing late in his study. Family, staff and his publisher were in and around the house that night.

public_briefing.opening_report: At 07:30 on Sunday, Iris Vell and groundskeeper Tomas Reed broke down the study door of Marcus Vell, 58, and found him dead at his desk. The door had been locked from the inside and the key was in his pocket. A half-finished cup of tea sat beside his keyboard. The island police have sealed the house and a court has been convened.
initial_leads: The cause of death is not yet confirmed.
Four people had contact with Marcus on the evening of the 9th.
The last ferry left the island at 22:10.

crime.method: Foxglove leaf extract mixed into Marcus's evening tea, delivered at about 21:40.
crime.motive: Marcus was ending Nora's contract and removing her co-writer credit on his latest novel, which she had largely ghostwritten.

true_timeline.event: Tomas fishes illegally at the pond.
Nora cuts foxglove leaves at the greenhouse bed. Tomas sees her from the pond.
Marcus and Iris argue about a divorce.
Marcus drafts a notice ending Nora's contract and removing her credit.
Nora leaves through the staff door (fob logged).
Iris starts a phone call with her sister in the sunroom.
Daniel leaves the house and drives to the Heron Inn.
Nora re-enters through the staff door, brews the poisoned tea.
Nora delivers the tea. Marcus later locks his study door from inside.
Daniel checks into the Heron Inn.
Nora leaves through the staff door (fob logged).
Nora boards the last ferry.
Marcus dies at his desk.
The door is broken down and the body found.

facts.statement: Marcus Vell was found dead at 07:30 in his study. The door was locked from the inside and the key was in his pocket.
Marcus died of cardiac-glycoside (foxglove) poisoning between 22:00 and 22:30.
Foxglove grows only in the greenhouse bed on the estate grounds.
At about 17:30 Nora Pike cut foxglove leaves at the greenhouse bed, wearing gardening gloves.
At 20:12 Marcus drafted a notice ending Nora's contract and removing her co-writer credit.
Nora's staff-door fob was used at 20:49 (exit), 21:31 (entry) and 22:04 (exit). No other fob used that door after 20:00.
Nora brewed and delivered Marcus's evening tea to the study at about 21:40.
Nora boarded the 22:10 ferry. The 21:00 ferry carried nobody from Vell House.
Iris was on a continuous phone call with her sister from 21:02 to 22:14, in the sunroom.
Daniel left the house at 21:15 and checked into the Heron Inn at 21:40.
Tomas was illegally fishing at the pond from 17:00 to 18:30.
Iris argued with Marcus about divorce at 19:30 and had consulted a divorce lawyer two weeks earlier.
Daniel's publishing house demanded repayment of an advance Marcus had not earned out.
Nora ghostwrote most of Marcus's latest novel, The Salt Road.

characters.name: Marcus Vell
characters.public_profile: A celebrated, demanding author known for working through the night with the door locked.

characters.name: Iris Vell
characters.public_profile: Marcus's wife of twenty-six years. The couple were known to be unhappy.

personality.speech_style: Clipped and formal; deflects with irony.

characters.claimed_alibi: In the sunroom on the phone with her sister from just after nine.
characters.true_whereabouts: In the sunroom on a continuous call from 21:02 to 22:14.

secrets.text: Two weeks ago she consulted a divorce lawyer.

testimony.told_answer: We argued about the divorce at half past seven. I am not proud of it, but I would never hurt him.
From just after nine I was in the sunroom on the phone with my sister.
Around half past nine I heard the kettle in the kitchen and assumed Marcus was making his own tea.

behavior.goal: Clear your name without exposing the divorce plans.

characters.name: Daniel Cruz
characters.public_profile: Marcus's long-time publisher, in the house for a dinner meeting about the next book.
characters.claimed_alibi: Left after dinner at about a quarter past nine and drove to the Heron Inn.
characters.true_whereabouts: Left at 21:15 and checked into the Heron Inn at 21:40.

secrets.text: His publishing house is close to insolvent and needed Marcus's final novel delivered.

testimony.told_answer: I left after dinner, about a quarter past nine, and drove to the Heron Inn.
My house wanted the advance back. That was business, nothing more.

behavior.goal: Protect the firm's reputation and avoid scandal.

characters.name: Nora Pike
characters.public_profile: Marcus's assistant for six years. Quiet, efficient, always at his side.

personality.speech_style: Polite, measured, answers only what is asked.

characters.claimed_alibi: Finished work at 20:45, left by the staff door, took the 21:00 ferry and never came back.
characters.true_whereabouts: Left at 20:49, returned at 21:31 to brew and deliver the poisoned tea, left at 22:04 and boarded the 22:10 ferry.

secrets.text: She poisoned Marcus with foxglove tea after learning he would erase her from the book she wrote.

testimony.told_answer: I finished at quarter to nine, left through the staff door and caught the nine o'clock ferry. I never came back.
Marcus made his own tea. I have not made it for him in months.
We had a few creative disagreements, nothing serious.
I do not go near the garden. I am allergic to pollen.

behavior.goal: Avoid conviction. Stay calm, stay consistent, never volunteer information.

breaking_point.note: Cracks when the lock log and the glove evidence are both put to her.

characters.name: Tomas Reed
characters.public_profile: Looked after the grounds for thirty years. Helped break down the study door.
characters.claimed_alibi: In the potting shed all afternoon, then home.
characters.true_whereabouts: Fishing illegally at the pond from 17:00 to 18:30, then home.

secrets.text: He poaches fish from the estate pond and fears losing his job.

testimony.told_answer: I was in the potting shed all afternoon.
Miss Pike was cutting leaves at the foxglove bed around half past five. I thought she was picking flowers for the study.

behavior.goal: Keep his job. Hide the poaching.

breaking_point.note: Admits fishing and then tells what he saw.

characters.name: Hana Lowe
characters.public_profile: Runs the ticket desk for the Heron Island ferry.
characters.claimed_alibi: Working the ticket desk.
characters.true_whereabouts: Working the ticket desk.

testimony.told_answer: The nine o'clock sailing carried nobody from Vell House. Ms. Pike boarded the 22:10 and said she was running late.

behavior.goal: Answer accurately and stay out of trouble.

locations.name: Marcus's study
locations.description: A book-lined room with a desk, a computer and a lockable oak door.

access.note: Sealed crime scene, open to investigators.

locations.name: Greenhouse and foxglove bed
locations.description: A walled bed of foxglove beside the greenhouse.

locations.name: Estate pond
locations.description: A reed-fringed pond behind the greenhouse.

locations.name: Nora's office
locations.description: A small office off the kitchen corridor.

evidence.name: Locked study door and key
evidence.description: The study door is locked from the inside. The only key was in Marcus Vell's trouser pocket. No sign of forced entry before the 07:30 break-in.
evidence.significance: Marcus locked the door himself, after the poison was already in him. Rules out 'someone entered the room later'.

evidence.name: Autopsy report
evidence.description: Cause of death: cardiac arrest from cardiac-glycoside poisoning. Time of death 22:00-22:30. Ingestion most likely 20-60 minutes before death.
evidence.significance: Fixes the poisoning window to roughly 21:00-22:10, which includes the 21:40 tea.

evidence.name: Teacup
evidence.description: A half-finished cup of tea on the desk with a green-brown sediment at the bottom.

forensic_result.result: The sediment contains foxglove leaf extract at a lethal concentration. The poison was in the tea.

evidence.significance: Shifts suspicion to whoever prepared and delivered the tea.

evidence.name: Unsent termination notice
evidence.description: An unsent email draft saved at 20:12: 'Nora - your contract ends this Friday, and your co-writer credit on The Salt Road will be removed from all future editions.'
evidence.significance: Motive. Alone it only shows she had a reason, not that she acted.

evidence.name: Staff-door lock log
evidence.description: Smart-lock log for the staff door: fob N.PIKE unlocked at 20:49 (exit), 21:31 (entry) and 22:04 (exit). No other fob used the door after 20:00.
evidence.significance: Destroys Nora's alibi: she came back at 21:31, right before the tea was delivered.

evidence.name: Ferry boarding log
evidence.description: Ferry ticket log: N. Pike boarded the 22:10 sailing. The 21:00 sailing carried nobody from Vell House.
evidence.significance: Second independent contradiction of Nora's 'I took the 21:00 ferry'.

evidence.name: Gloves and pruning shears
evidence.description: A pair of green-stained gardening gloves and small pruning shears in the bottom drawer of Nora Pike's desk.

forensic_result.result: The stains and blade residue are fresh foxglove sap.

evidence.significance: Physical link between Nora and the poison source.

evidence.name: Hidden fishing gear
evidence.description: A hidden fishing rod, bucket and fish scales in the reeds at the pond. The bucket tag reads 'T.R.'.
evidence.significance: Not the murder. It exposes Tomas's lie about his whereabouts and pressures him into telling what he saw.

evidence.name: Iris's phone records
evidence.description: Mobile records: Iris Vell on a continuous call with her sister from 21:02 to 22:14, connected through the house Wi-Fi in the sunroom area.
evidence.significance: Supports Iris's alibi for the poisoning window. Does not by itself prove her innocence.

evidence.name: Heron Inn register
evidence.description: Heron Inn register: D. Cruz checked in at 21:40 and paid for the night. The night clerk recalls him arriving wet from the rain.
evidence.significance: Daniel was off the premises before the tea was made.

evidence.name: Tomas's eyewitness statement
evidence.description: Tomas Reed states that at about 17:30 he saw Nora Pike cutting leaves from the foxglove bed by the greenhouse, wearing gardening gloves.
evidence.significance: Places Nora at the poison source. Reliability is reduced because Tomas lied earlier.

seats.note: One per suspect. The court appoints a house-bot defender if a charged suspect has none at trial.

key_evidence_chain.inference: Marcus locked the door himself and died of foxglove poisoning, so the poison was ingested before he locked up.
The poison was in the evening tea, so the poisoner is whoever prepared or delivered it.
Nora Pike lied about leaving at 20:45. She re-entered at 21:31 and left at 22:04, boarding the 22:10 ferry.
Nora cut foxglove at 17:30, and gloves and shears with fresh foxglove sap were in her desk.
Motive: Marcus ended her contract and removed her credit that evening.

wrong_conclusions.why_tempting: Public argument about divorce hours before; stood to benefit; discovered the body.
wrong_conclusions.why_wrong: On a continuous phone call during the tea window and never used the staff door.

wrong_conclusions.why_tempting: Money dispute over the advance and a nervous manner.
wrong_conclusions.why_wrong: Left at 21:15 and was checked into the inn at 21:40, before the tea was made.

wrong_conclusions.why_tempting: Controls the garden, lied about where he was, hid fishing gear.
wrong_conclusions.why_wrong: No motive, no staff-door fob, and his lie hid poaching. His testimony actually points to Nora.

solver_check.notes: Run the solver agent before publishing.

conclusion.judge_reasoning_template: The poison was delivered in the evening tea (EV-103). The staff-door log and ferry log show the defendant returned to the house at 21:31 after claiming to have left for good (EV-105, EV-106). She had cut foxglove that afternoon and kept the stained tools in her desk (EV-111, EV-107). She had a motive from the termination notice (EV-104). No other suspect had both access and opportunity.
conclusion.reveal_narration: Nora Pike had written most of The Salt Road and was about to be erased from it. After Marcus told her, she slipped out at 20:49, then came back at 21:31 through the staff door, brewed foxglove leaves into his tea and carried it to the study. Marcus, a creature of habit, locked the door behind her. By the time the poison worked, Nora was on the 22:10 ferry with an alibi she had rehearsed.
conclusion.epilogue: The Salt Road was reissued with both names on the cover.

bonuses.condition: Names Nora Pike in submit_theory before the charging phase.
Shows the court why the evidence against an innocent client is weak.

cases.title: The Sapphire Lantern
cases.tagline: Four minutes of darkness, one empty display case, and a key that was in two places at once.
cases.author: Interrogation Room Team

setting.location: Marlowe Museum of Antiquities, Grand Gallery
setting.atmosphere: A charity gala for 200 guests, with a string quartet and champagne in the atrium.
setting.summary: The museum's star exhibit, a jewelled 15th-century lamp, vanished during a short power failure at its own gala.

public_briefing.opening_report: At 21:14 during the Marlowe Museum's charity gala the gallery lights failed for four minutes. When power returned the display case holding the Sapphire Lantern, insured for 4.2 million, was open and empty. Curator Beatrice Lang had been on the atrium stage giving her speech to 200 guests. Nobody saw the thief. The board has asked the court to convene.
initial_leads: The display case shows no sign of forced entry.
The power failed at 21:10 and returned at 21:14.
Several people had reasons to be near the gallery.

crime.method: The real lantern was swapped for a resin replica on 2 March and shipped to Antwerp on 11 March. The blackout 'theft' of the replica was staged to hide the swap and trigger an insurance claim.
crime.motive: Curator Beatrice Lang was in deep debt and had a private buyer abroad.

true_timeline.event: Beatrice commissions a resin replica of the lantern.
Beatrice removes the lantern for 'cleaning' and puts the replica in the case.
The real lantern is shipped to Antwerp as 'restoration materials'. Beatrice pays Felix 6,000 for the plan.
Beatrice hands her case key to Felix.
Beatrice begins her speech on the atrium stage.
Omar leaves his post to take a bookmaker's call.
Felix overloads service socket S-4 and trips the gallery circuit.
Felix wheels a catering cart into the gallery, opens the case with the curator's key and takes the replica.
Felix leaves with a covered tray.
Power is restored. The case is found empty.
Felix returns the key to Beatrice.

facts.statement: The display case was opened with the curator's key at 21:11. There was no forced entry.
Beatrice Lang was on the atrium stage giving a speech from 21:00 to 21:20.
The gallery lights failed from 21:10 to 21:14 because of an overload on service socket S-4 in the catering corridor.
A Moreau & Co. catering cart entered the gallery at 21:11 and left at 21:13 with a covered tray.
Beatrice gave her case key to Felix Moreau at 20:55 and took it back at 21:30.
On 11 March Beatrice paid Felix 6,000 through Lang Heritage Consulting.
On 28 February Beatrice commissioned a full-scale resin replica of the lantern.
On 2 March the real lantern was swapped for the replica. On 11 March it was shipped to Antwerp in a crate marked 'restoration materials'.
Omar Haddad left his post from 21:09 to 21:15 to take a call from a bookmaker.
Lady Cordelia Ashby offered 2.5 million for the lantern last year and was refused.
After 2 March, Beatrice postponed the insurance re-appraisal twice.

characters.name: Beatrice Lang
characters.public_profile: The museum's respected curator of fifteen years and the face of the Sapphire Lantern exhibit.

personality.speech_style: Articulate, speaks in complete paragraphs, never raises her voice.

characters.claimed_alibi: On the atrium stage giving the gala speech.
characters.true_whereabouts: On the atrium stage from 21:00 to 21:20, which is true. The crime was carried out by her accomplice.

secrets.text: She swapped the lantern for a replica, shipped the real one abroad and staged the theft for the insurance payout.

testimony.told_answer: I was on the atrium stage giving my speech. Two hundred people saw me.
My case key never left my person all evening.
A routine annual cleaning on 2 March. Nothing unusual.
My personal finances are none of your business.

behavior.goal: Avoid conviction. Her speech alibi is real, so keep calm and let the evidence chain prove the conspiracy.

breaking_point.note: Cracks when the freight booking and the replica invoice are put together.

characters.name: Felix Moreau
characters.public_profile: Runs the premium catering firm hired for the gala. Charming, always in a hurry.

personality.speech_style: Jokes to deflect; sweats when pressed.

characters.claimed_alibi: In the kitchen supervising service all evening.
characters.true_whereabouts: In the service corridor and gallery between 21:10 and 21:13.

secrets.text: He overloaded the socket and took the replica from the case with the curator's key for a 6,000 payment.

testimony.told_answer: My staff stayed in the kitchen all night. Nobody from my company went into the gallery.
That payment was for extra event staffing.

behavior.goal: Avoid conviction. Protect himself first; he will flip if offered leniency.

breaking_point.note: Names Beatrice if the prosecutor offers a lesser charge.

characters.name: Omar Haddad
characters.public_profile: Guards the gallery door at events. Reliable on paper, with a gambling habit nobody mentions.
characters.claimed_alibi: At his post the whole time.
characters.true_whereabouts: Left his post from 21:09 to 21:15 for a phone call.

secrets.text: He left his post to take a call from a bookmaker and owes 18,000.

testimony.told_answer: I was at my post the whole time.

behavior.goal: Hide the gambling and keep his job.

breaking_point.note: Admits the call. Denies anything to do with the theft.

characters.name: Lady Cordelia Ashby
characters.public_profile: A wealthy collector who has openly coveted the Sapphire Lantern for years.

personality.speech_style: Grand and amused; speaks as if everyone works for her.

characters.claimed_alibi: In the front row of the atrium listening to the speech.
characters.true_whereabouts: In the front row from 21:00 to 21:20.

testimony.told_answer: Yes, I offered 2.5 million last year and was refused. I sat in the front row for the speech with a glass of champagne.

behavior.goal: Clear her name and make sure the lantern is found.

characters.name: Priya Nair
characters.public_profile: Appraised the lantern for the museum's insurer in February.
characters.claimed_alibi: Attending the gala as the insurer's guest.
characters.true_whereabouts: Attending the gala.

testimony.told_answer: After the 2 March cleaning I asked to re-weigh the lantern. Ms. Lang postponed it twice.

behavior.goal: Answer accurately.

locations.name: Grand Gallery
locations.description: A marble hall with the display case at its centre.

locations.name: Catering service corridor
locations.description: A back corridor linking the kitchen to the gallery, with a battery-backed camera.

locations.name: Power room
locations.description: Breaker boards and the building's power log.

locations.name: Security room
locations.description: Guard post logs and the key safe.

locations.name: Curator's office
locations.description: Beatrice Lang's private office and filing cabinets.

evidence.name: Display case lock log
evidence.description: The case's electronic lock log shows it was opened at 21:11 using the CURATOR key. There was no forced entry, and the security-safe key was never checked out.
evidence.significance: The curator's key was used at 21:11 while she was on stage, so someone else held it. Points to a conspiracy.

evidence.name: Gallery breaker log
evidence.description: The main gallery circuit tripped at 21:10 and was reset at 21:14. The trip was caused by an overload on service socket S-4 in the catering corridor.
evidence.significance: The blackout was engineered from the catering side.

evidence.name: Corridor camera footage
evidence.description: A backup-battery camera records a catering cart tagged 'Moreau & Co.' entering the gallery at 21:11 and leaving at 21:13 with a covered tray. The person's face is not visible.
evidence.significance: Puts Felix's company in the gallery during the blackout.

evidence.name: Payment from Lang Heritage Consulting
evidence.description: On 11 March, Lang Heritage Consulting transferred 6,000 to Moreau & Co. with the reference 'event extras'. Company filings list Beatrice Lang as its sole director.
evidence.significance: Money trail linking the curator to the caterer.

evidence.name: Freight booking to Antwerp
evidence.description: On 11 March a crate labelled 'restoration materials' was collected from the museum loading dock, booked by B. Lang, destination Antwerp, declared weight 6.5 kg.
evidence.significance: The real lantern left the building three days before the 'theft'.

evidence.name: Replica casting invoice
evidence.description: Kline Casting Studio invoice dated 28 February: one full-scale resin replica of the Sapphire Lantern with gem-effect finish, ordered by B. Lang and paid from the museum's discretionary account.
evidence.significance: Proves a replica existed before the gala. What was 'stolen' was a copy.

evidence.name: Security post log and call records
evidence.description: The post log shows Omar Haddad left the gallery door post at 21:09 and returned at 21:15. His phone shows a five-minute call to a betting line, and a payment reminder shows a debt of 18,000.
evidence.significance: Suspicious but unrelated. Omar never held a case key and has no link to the money trail.

evidence.name: Assessor's file note
evidence.description: Assessor Priya Nair's file note: after the 2 March 'cleaning' the curator postponed the lantern's re-appraisal twice and refused a re-weigh.
evidence.significance: Shows Beatrice was avoiding anything that would expose the swap.

key_evidence_chain.inference: The case was opened with the curator's key at 21:11 while Beatrice was on stage, so she gave the key to someone: this is an inside job with an accomplice.
The blackout was engineered from the catering corridor and a Moreau & Co. cart entered the gallery: the accomplice is Felix.
Beatrice paid Felix 6,000 through her own consulting company.
The real lantern was shipped abroad on 11 March, a replica was ordered on 28 February and the re-appraisal was blocked: the 'theft' stole a copy.

wrong_conclusions.why_tempting: Left his post exactly during the blackout and owes money to a bookmaker.
wrong_conclusions.why_wrong: The case opened with the curator's key, which he never held, and no money flowed to him.

wrong_conclusions.why_tempting: Openly wanted the lantern and could afford to buy it.
wrong_conclusions.why_wrong: In the front row during the speech, with no access to keys or the service corridor. The real lantern was shipped to a buyer in Antwerp.

solver_check.notes: Run the solver agent before publishing.

expected_verdicts.charge: Theft by deception and insurance fraud

conclusion.judge_reasoning_template: The case was opened with the curator's key while the curator was on stage (EV-201). A Moreau & Co. cart entered during a blackout triggered from the catering corridor (EV-202, EV-203), and Beatrice Lang paid Moreau & Co. through her own company (EV-204). The real lantern had left the museum on 11 March (EV-205) and a replica had been commissioned on 28 February (EV-206).
conclusion.reveal_narration: Beatrice Lang swapped the Sapphire Lantern for a resin copy on 2 March and shipped the real one to a buyer in Antwerp. To collect the insurance she needed a theft, so she handed her key to Felix Moreau, who overloaded a socket, wheeled a cart into the dark gallery and carried away the copy. Her speech alibi was perfect. It was the key that gave her away.
conclusion.epilogue: The lantern was recovered in Antwerp. The museum's insurer withdrew from the claim.

bonuses.condition: Identifies Felix as an accomplice before the trial phase.
Obtains Felix's testimony against Beatrice through a lawful deal.

cases.title: Orion Down
cases.tagline: The company's flagship database was deleted at 2 a.m. by someone who was fast asleep.
cases.author: Interrogation Room Team

setting.location: Northwind Analytics, 6th-floor engineering office and server room
setting.atmosphere: A product launch is 48 hours away and everybody is exhausted.
setting.summary: A staff-run internal tribunal investigates how the production database was deleted.

public_briefing.opening_report: At 02:14 on Tuesday the production database 'Orion', which powers Northwind's flagship product, was deleted, and the latest backups were found corrupted. The audit log shows the deletion was run using the credentials of DevOps lead Sara Okafor. The launch is in 48 hours and Northwind has convened an internal tribunal.
initial_leads: The deletion used Sara Okafor's account.
The backups were corrupted by the same session.
Several people had grievances or access.

crime.method: Kenji phished Sara's SSO credentials, then connected his laptop to the guest Wi-Fi from the loading dock and ran the deletion and backup corruption using her account.
crime.motive: Retaliation for the non-renewal of his contract, using access that IT had not yet revoked.

true_timeline.event: Ravi terminates Kenji's contract effective Monday.
Kenji registers a fake SSO site using a personal alias.
Sara enters her credentials on the fake SSO page and tells nobody.
A ticket backlog delays removal of Kenji's building and guest-network access until Wednesday.
Judith attends a board call, then goes to sleep.
Sara falls asleep at home.
Leo finally leaves the office after gaming on a dev server.
Kenji's car enters the garage.
Kenji's laptop joins the guest Wi-Fi.
Orion is deleted using Sara's credentials. Backups are corrupted at 02:16.
Kenji's car leaves the garage.

facts.statement: Orion was deleted at 02:14 by Sara's credentials from IP 10.20.7.88 on the guest Wi-Fi, and the latest backups were corrupted at 02:16 by the same session.
Sara was asleep at home from 23:10 to 06:30.
On 30 Aug Sara entered her credentials on a phishing page and told nobody.
The phishing site was registered by an account tied to Kenji's consulting alias.
IP 10.20.7.88 was leased to Kenji's laptop from 01:35 to 02:40.
Kenji's car entered the garage at 01:20 and left at 02:50. His badge shows he left the building at 18:05 and did not badge back in.
Kenji's contract was terminated on Friday. His access should have ended Monday but IT delayed revocation until Wednesday.
Judith Mann wrote a memo proposing to retire Orion if hosting costs rise another 20%.
Leo stayed at the office until 23:30 and keeps the staging-server password on a sticky note.
Judith attended a board call from 22:00 to 22:45 and then went to sleep.

characters.name: Sara Okafor
characters.public_profile: Runs the infrastructure team and owns the production credentials the audit log points at.
characters.claimed_alibi: Asleep at home all night.
characters.true_whereabouts: Asleep at home from 23:10 to 06:30.

secrets.text: She clicked a phishing link and entered her password, and was too embarrassed to report it.

testimony.told_answer: I was asleep at home all night. My watch will prove it.
I am careful. I never click unknown links.

behavior.goal: Clear your name. You are afraid the phishing click was your fault.

breaking_point.note: Admits the click once the phishing email is shown.

characters.name: Leo Park
characters.public_profile: A talented intern with a reputation for staying late and breaking things in staging.
characters.claimed_alibi: Left at seven and gamed at home.
characters.true_whereabouts: Stayed in the office until 23:30 playing on a dev server, then went home.

secrets.text: He stayed late gaming on a dev server, against policy.

testimony.told_answer: I left at seven and was gaming at home.
That is the staging password. It does not work on production.

behavior.goal: Avoid getting fired for the gaming.

characters.name: Judith Mann
characters.public_profile: Controls the budget and has openly complained about Orion's hosting costs.
characters.claimed_alibi: On a board call until 22:45, then asleep.
characters.true_whereabouts: Board call 22:00-22:45, then asleep at home.

testimony.told_answer: A routine budgeting memo. I would never sabotage our own flagship.
Board call until 22:45, then I went to bed.

behavior.goal: Defend your reputation and the launch.

characters.name: Kenji Watanabe
characters.public_profile: A skilled contractor who helped build Orion. His contract was not renewed last Friday.

personality.speech_style: Soft-spoken and exact; says 'with respect' before disagreeing.

characters.claimed_alibi: Home all night. His badge shows he left at 18:05.
characters.true_whereabouts: In the loading dock with a laptop from 01:35 to 02:40.

secrets.text: He phished Sara's credentials and deleted Orion from the loading dock as revenge.

testimony.told_answer: I was home all night. My badge shows I left at 18:05.
I was disappointed, but I handled it professionally.
I never had any way into Sara's account.

behavior.goal: Avoid conviction. Rely on the fact that the log names Sara, and never admit to being on site.

breaking_point.note: Cracks when the guest-network lease and garage log are both put to him.

characters.name: Ravi Menon
characters.public_profile: Technical head of Northwind and the complainant in the tribunal.
characters.claimed_alibi: At home.
characters.true_whereabouts: At home.

testimony.told_answer: I ended Kenji's contract on Friday. His access should have been cut on Monday, but the ticket queue delayed it until Wednesday.

behavior.goal: Give the tribunal accurate information.

locations.name: Server room
locations.description: The room hosting the audit console and production systems.

locations.name: Loading dock
locations.description: A back area covered by the guest Wi-Fi and a camera that was switched off for maintenance.

locations.name: Finance office
locations.description: Judith Mann's office and shared finance drive.

locations.name: Intern desk
locations.description: Leo Park's cluttered workstation.

evidence.name: Orion audit log
evidence.description: Audit log: at 02:14 user sara.okafor ran DROP DATABASE orion from IP 10.20.7.88 on the guest network. At 02:16 the same session corrupted the latest backups.
evidence.significance: Points at Sara, but the source IP is on the GUEST network, which an engineer at a desk would not use.

evidence.name: Sara's sleep and Wi-Fi data
evidence.description: Sara's smartwatch shows her asleep from 23:10 to 06:30, and her phone stayed on her home Wi-Fi all night.

discovery.record_source: Personal smartwatch and home router records (Sara Okafor)

evidence.significance: Sara was not at the keyboard, so someone else used her credentials.

evidence.name: Phishing email and fake SSO page
evidence.description: On 30 Aug Sara received an email from it-support@northwind-sso.help urging her to re-verify her login on a look-alike SSO page.

forensic_result.result: The fake SSO site was registered on 29 Aug, the day Kenji's contract ended. The hosting account's recovery email is kenji.w.consulting.

evidence.significance: Shows how the credentials were stolen and ties the attack infrastructure to Kenji's alias.

evidence.name: Guest Wi-Fi lease and asset register
evidence.description: IP 10.20.7.88 was leased from 01:35 to 02:40 to a laptop whose MAC address matches the contractor laptop registered to Kenji Watanabe.
evidence.significance: Identifies the device that ran the deletion.

evidence.name: Garage plate-reader log
evidence.description: Kenji Watanabe's car entered the garage at 01:20 and left at 02:50. His badge shows he left the building at 18:05 and did not badge back in.
evidence.significance: Places Kenji physically on site and breaks his 'I was home' claim.

evidence.name: Termination letter and delayed revocation
evidence.description: Letter dated Friday 29 Aug ending Kenji Watanabe's contract on Monday. A ticket backlog delayed removal of his building and guest-network privileges until Wednesday.
evidence.significance: Motive and opportunity: grievance plus access that should have been revoked.

evidence.name: CFO's cost-cutting memo
evidence.description: Memo from Judith Mann proposing to retire Orion if hosting costs rise another 20%.
evidence.significance: A business opinion, not a motive for sabotaging the launch she wants to succeed.

evidence.name: Sticky note with a password
evidence.description: A sticky note on Leo Park's monitor holds a password. It is the shared staging-server password, which does not work on production.
evidence.significance: Poor hygiene, not sabotage. Staging credentials cannot touch production.

key_evidence_chain.inference: The deletion used Sara's account from the guest network while Sara was asleep at home: her credentials were stolen.
A phishing page harvested her credentials, and its hosting account traces back to Kenji's consulting alias.
The guest-network IP was leased to Kenji's laptop, and his car was in the garage from 01:20 to 02:50, contradicting his claim of being home.
His contract had just ended and IT had not yet revoked his access: motive and opportunity.

wrong_conclusions.why_tempting: The audit log names her account.
wrong_conclusions.why_wrong: She was asleep at home, the source IP was on the guest network, and her credentials had been phished.

wrong_conclusions.why_tempting: A password on a sticky note and a lie about when he left.
wrong_conclusions.why_wrong: The note is a staging password that cannot access production, and the deletion came from Kenji's device.

wrong_conclusions.why_tempting: Wrote a memo about retiring Orion.
wrong_conclusions.why_wrong: The memo is a routine budgeting suggestion, she was on a board call and asleep, and nothing ties her to the guest network.

solver_check.notes: Run the solver agent before publishing.

conclusion.judge_reasoning_template: The deletion ran from a guest-network IP (EV-301) that was leased to Kenji's registered laptop (EV-304) while his car was in the garage (EV-305). Sara was asleep at home (EV-302) and her credentials were phished through a site traceable to Kenji's alias (EV-303). His contract had just ended and his access was still live (EV-306).
conclusion.reveal_narration: Kenji Watanabe built a fake single-sign-on page the night his contract ended and waited for someone to bite. Sara did, and told nobody. When IT failed to revoke his guest-network access, he came back at 1:20 a.m., sat in the loading dock with his laptop and deleted Orion with her password. He was careful to leave his badge unused. He forgot the garage cameras and the Wi-Fi lease.
conclusion.epilogue: Backups from an offline snapshot restored Orion with six hours to spare. IT now reviews contractor access on the day a contract ends.

bonuses.condition: Clears Sara Okafor by showing the log was produced through stolen credentials.
Runs the domain trace that links the phishing site to Kenji's alias.

cases.title: The Clockwork Heist
cases.tagline: An irreplaceable astrolabe cog disappears from the Victorian clocktower at the stroke of midnight.
cases.author: Interrogation Room Guild

setting.atmosphere: Fog rolling over cobblestones. The immense pendulum echoes every sixty seconds.
setting.summary: During the annual chimes restoration, the gilded astronomical gear was substituted with a soft lead replica.

public_briefing.opening_report: At 00:05, head horologist Tobias Vance reported that the master golden gear was missing from the turret room. The replacement lead duplicate halted the chime gears at 00:02. Two apprentices and a conservator were present in the tower that evening.
initial_leads: The turret room requires a brass key held only by the tower master.
The duplicate gear bore fresh machine-oil residue.
A black velvet pouch was found dropped by the lower belfry.

crime.method: Swapped the golden gear for a lead replica during the midnight chime maintenance.
crime.motive: Sell the antique timepiece gear to a private overseas buyer to clear debts.

true_timeline.event: Tobias finishes the evening windup.
Felix swaps the golden gear for the lead replica.
Beatrice hears strange metallic grinding in the shafts.
The chimes jam as the lead gear teeth shear off.

facts.statement: The astronomical golden gear was intact in its casing during the 22:30 windup.
Felix Croft possessed a duplicate lathe tool matching the lead gear cuts.
Traces of synthetic turret lubricant were found on Felix's apron.
Beatrice observed someone descending from the turret five minutes before midnight.
The lead gear sheared at 00:02, establishing the exact minute the clock seized.

characters.name: Tobias Vance
characters.public_profile: Senior keeper of the town clocktower, meticulous and protective of the mechanism.

characters.name: Felix Croft
characters.public_profile: Ambitious young mechanic who studied precision engineering in Zurich.

personality.speech_style: Technical terminology used as a shield.

characters.claimed_alibi: Polishing the pendulum weights in the sub-basement between 23:30 and 00:15.
characters.true_whereabouts: In the turret chamber executing the swap and concealing the gold gear in his toolbox.

secrets.text: He owes 5,000 sovereigns to high-stakes street bookmakers.

testimony.told_answer: I was downstairs in the sub-basement buffing brass weights when the clock stopped.
My apron gets stained with oil every day during standard workshop maintenance.

behavior.goal: Deflect attention toward visiting collectors.

breaking_point.note: Admits where the gold gear is stashed.

characters.name: Beatrice Thorne
characters.public_profile: Visiting inspector assessing the heritage clockwork for the regional museum.
characters.claimed_alibi: Cataloging brass plates in the mid-belfry.
characters.true_whereabouts: In the mid-belfry, saw Felix slip down the ladder.

testimony.told_answer: I heard urgent footsteps descending the turret ladder at 23:55, followed by heavy metallic clanking.

behavior.goal: Ensure the historic gear is recovered safely.

locations.description: The apex of the clocktower containing the escapement wheel and main dial drives.

locations.description: Felix Croft's designated repair desk lined with micro-lathes and metal filings.

evidence.description: A soft lead copy of the master cog, deformed under the pendulum load at 00:02.
evidence.significance: Proves that the gear was intentionally duplicated and switched before midnight.

forensic_result.result: Lead alloy cast using a molding compound and hand-filed teeth.

evidence.name: Custom Carbide File
evidence.description: A Swiss-cut finishing file with lead powder matching the replica gear teeth.
evidence.significance: Direct physical tool link showing Felix shaped the replacement lead gear teeth.

evidence.name: Oiled Apprentice Apron
evidence.description: Heavy canvas apron bearing grease and micro-flecks of gilded gold foil.
evidence.significance: Chemical transfer of specialized high-viscosity turret lubricant.

evidence.name: Dropped Black Pouch
evidence.description: Drawstring velvet pouch found dropped behind the belfry bell mountings.
evidence.significance: Red herring containing common clock oil bottles, dropped during flight.

key_evidence_chain.inference: The gear was intentionally duplicated and swapped before midnight.
Felix shaped the lead teeth on his lathe and handled the turret lubricants.

wrong_conclusions.why_tempting: Beatrice was cataloging antiquities near the belfry and had market knowledge.
wrong_conclusions.why_wrong: She had no access to the workshop lathe tools or gear lubricants.

solver_check.notes: Carbide lathe filings directly contradict Felix's alibi.

conclusion.judge_reasoning_template: The tribunal finds Felix Croft guilty based on lathe residue (EV-402) and turret lubricant transfer (EV-403).
conclusion.reveal_narration: Felix Croft admitted to concealing the authentic gilded astrolabe gear inside his toolbox compartment.
conclusion.epilogue: The astronomical astrolabe was returned to St. Jude's Belltower. Felix was sentenced to restitution labor.

conclusion.reveal_narration: Confronted with the camera timestamp gap, Jax Thorne extracted the quantum chip from his boot heel.

cases.author: Heritage Crime Squad

setting.atmosphere: Crystal chandeliers, string quartet playing softly, masked patrons sipping champagne.
setting.summary: The celebrated portrait 'Lady with a Falcon' was replaced by an acrylic replica on aged canvas.

public_briefing.opening_report: At 22:30, curator Henri Dupont noticed that the varnish on the newly unveiled Renaissance canvas was dry to the touch under ultraviolet inspection. The authentic painting had been removed from its gilded frame.
initial_leads: The painting frame was unbolted from the rear service corridor.
A restorer's pigment box was found in the coat check.
The security laser curtain had been temporarily paused for catering trolley transit.

stolen_items: Lady with a Falcon Oil Painting
crime.method: Unlatched frame from the rear service recess during the catering break and swapped the canvas.
crime.motive: Sell the original to an anonymous offshore collector to save her failing private studio.

true_timeline.event: Henri unveils the genuine painting.
Camille slips into the rear service corridor with canvas tube.
Lord Ashford drinks champagne near the display.
UV inspection exposes the forgery.

facts.statement: The genuine Renaissance canvas was safely displayed at 20:00.
Camille Laurent had special access to the rear frame service latch.
Lord Ashford was in conversation with Henri between 21:50 and 22:20.
The forgery used synthetic phthalocyanine blue unknown in the 16th century.

characters.public_profile: Distinguished art historian and director of the Galerie Royale.

characters.name: Camille Laurent
characters.public_profile: Gifted conservator who prepared the exhibition's antique gilt frames.
characters.claimed_alibi: Socializing in the garden courtyard from 21:30 until 22:15.
characters.true_whereabouts: Behind the rear display wall swapping the canvas off its stretcher bars.

secrets.text: She painted the replica over four months in her home atelier.

testimony.told_answer: I spent the entire hour after nine-thirty admiring the courtyard sculpture by the fountain.
I only use period-accurate tempera and rabbit-skin glue for all museum commissions.

behavior.goal: Convince the court that the painting was taken by an international ring.

characters.public_profile: Wealthy museum trustee who had made an unsuccessful bid to acquire the painting.
characters.claimed_alibi: Speaking with Henri and other patrons in the center gallery.
characters.true_whereabouts: In the center gallery in plain view of forty witnesses.

testimony.told_answer: Henri and I were discussing my endowment pledge in the center of the room.

behavior.goal: Preserve his aristocratic standing.

locations.name: Rear Service Corridor
locations.description: Concealed technician passage providing access behind the display walls.

locations.description: On-site conservation studio with easels and solvent bottles.

evidence.description: Ultraviolet fluorescence report showing modern synthetic blue pigment beneath the varnish.
evidence.significance: Scientifically proves the exhibited canvas was painted recently.

evidence.significance: Shatters Camille's garden alibi with hard electronic timestamps.

evidence.name: Synthetic Phthalo Pigment Jar
evidence.description: A partially used jar of synthetic blue pigment in Camille's travel kit.
evidence.significance: Direct chemical match with the pigments found on the forged canvas.

evidence.description: A rejected formal written offer of three million euros for the painting.
evidence.significance: Explains Lord Ashford's motive, but he lacked the forgery craft and access.

seats.note: Argues art fraud and grand larceny.

Camille accessed the rear frame during the window with matching pigments.

wrong_conclusions.why_tempting: Lord Ashford had the money and was desperate to own the painting.
wrong_conclusions.why_wrong: He had an ironclad public alibi and possessed no technical forgery skill.

solver_check.notes: Keycard audit EV-602 breaks the garden alibi completely.

conclusion.judge_reasoning_template: The tribunal finds Camille Laurent guilty based on matching modern pigment (EV-601, EV-603) and timestamped access to the rear frame latch (EV-602).
conclusion.reveal_narration: Camille Laurent confessed that the authentic Renaissance canvas was packed inside an insulated mailing tube at the local courier hub.
conclusion.epilogue: The masterpiece was recovered without damage and re-hung under laser vibration sensors.

bonuses.condition: Match synthetic pigment chemistry in trial
